claims.text: The starting feedstock is untreated AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder with irregular oxide content.
Resonant acoustic mixing can coat AlCrFeNiSi powder particles with a uniform, controlled layer of nanoscale oxide particles.
Yttrium oxide is a candidate nanoscale dispersoid for the powder coating.
Laser powder bed fusion can incorporate and disperse the pre-deposited nanoscale oxides throughout the consolidated build.
The nano-oxide dispersion will refine the grains in AlCrFeNiSi.
The nano-oxide dispersion will moderate thermal stress during processing.
The dispersoids will pin grain boundaries and thereby stabilize the refined microstructure.
The dispersoids will pin dislocations in the solidified material.
The pre-deposited oxides will distribute and reduce local thermal gradients during laser powder bed fusion.
The oxides will interrupt rapid grain growth during solidification.
Reducing thermal gradients and pinning microstructural defects will minimize residual-stress accumulation.
Dispersion strengthening can improve the balance of strength and ductility relative to an untreated alloy.
Oxide-coated AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual stress than components made from untreated powder under conventional high-thermal-load conditions.
Oxide-coated AlCrFeNiSi components will have finer and more uniform grains than the baseline components.
Oxide-coated AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit higher yield strength and improved ductility than the baseline components.
The proposed geometry is a miniature laser-powder-bed-fused component approximately 10 × 10 × 2 mm.
Processing uses moderate laser power and scan speed, an inert atmosphere, and interlayer preheating around 200 °C.
Interlayer preheating around 200 °C will stabilize the melt pool while retaining a lower overall thermal load than conventional settings.
The expected improvement applies primarily to miniature laser-powder-bed-fused components, while larger builds and other additive-manufacturing methods may require additional optimization.

Residual stress, grain structure, yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility can be compared between coated-powder and untreated-powder groups using X-ray diffraction, EBSD, and micro-tensile testing under otherwise identical processing parameters.

contradictions.description: The stated prediction and baseline compare coated material processed at lower/moderate thermal load with untreated material under conventional high-thermal-load parameters, whereas the falsification experiment requires coated and untreated groups to use identical parameters. Thus the experiment does not directly test the stated conventional-high-load comparator.
